course_title: Use of Library and Study Skills

questions.question_text: The primary purpose of an academic library is to:
questions.explanation: Academic libraries support teaching, learning, research, and access to scholarly information.

questions.question_text: A library is best described as:

options.label: A
options.text: An organised collection of information resources and services

options.label: C
options.text: A place used only for silent reading

questions.explanation: A library combines organised information resources, services, systems, and facilities.

questions.question_text: Which group is commonly served by a university library?

options.label: B
options.text: Only visitors from outside the university

questions.explanation: University libraries primarily support members of the academic community.

questions.question_text: Which activity is normally part of library service?
questions.explanation: Reference and information assistance are core library services.

questions.question_text: A library user's ability to locate and use resources effectively is known as:
questions.explanation: Library literacy involves understanding how to find and use library resources and services.

questions.question_text: Why are libraries important to independent learning?

options.label: A
options.text: They provide organised access to diverse sources beyond classroom teaching

options.label: C
options.text: They guarantee every source is correct

options.label: D
options.text: They eliminate the need for studying

questions.explanation: Libraries broaden access to information and support self-directed study and research.

questions.question_text: A library established mainly to support a university is called a:
questions.explanation: Academic libraries serve universities, colleges, and other tertiary institutions.

questions.question_text: A public library primarily serves:
questions.explanation: Public libraries provide information and reading services to the wider community.

questions.question_text: The National Library of a country commonly has responsibility for:
questions.explanation: National libraries preserve and document a country's published intellectual heritage.

questions.question_text: A special library is usually established to:

options.label: A
options.text: Serve the specialised information needs of an organisation or profession

questions.explanation: Special libraries focus on particular subject areas, organisations, or professional groups.

questions.question_text: Which library is most closely associated with a secondary school?
questions.explanation: School libraries support pupils and teachers within primary or secondary schools.

questions.question_text: A research institute requiring highly specialised scientific journals would most likely depend on a:
questions.explanation: Special libraries are designed around focused professional or research information needs.

questions.question_text: Library classification is used mainly to:
questions.explanation: Classification groups materials by subject so they can be arranged and retrieved systematically.

questions.question_text: A call number is used to:

options.label: A
options.text: Identify the location of a library item on the shelves

options.label: B
options.text: Show the selling price of a book

questions.explanation: A call number represents the item's classified location in the library.

questions.question_text: Which classification system is widely used in libraries?
questions.explanation: The Dewey Decimal Classification is a widely used library classification system.

questions.question_text: In a classified library, books on similar subjects are generally:

options.label: C
options.text: Kept only at the circulation desk

questions.explanation: Classification groups related subjects together to support browsing and retrieval.

questions.question_text: Why is classification useful to a student?

options.label: A
options.text: It helps locate materials and browse related subjects

options.label: C
options.text: It prevents books from being borrowed

questions.explanation: Classification provides predictable locations and groups related subject material.

questions.question_text: Two books with similar call numbers are most likely to:
questions.explanation: Call numbers principally reflect subject classification, so similar numbers often indicate related subjects.

questions.question_text: A library catalogue is primarily used to:

options.label: A
options.text: Find materials held by a library

questions.explanation: A catalogue provides searchable records of resources owned or accessible through a library.

questions.question_text: A catalogue search by author is most useful when:
questions.explanation: An author search retrieves works associated with a known creator.

questions.question_text: OPAC stands for:
questions.explanation: OPAC means Online Public Access Catalogue.

questions.question_text: A subject search in an OPAC helps a user:

options.label: A
options.text: Find materials related to a topic

options.label: B
options.text: Locate only books by one author

questions.explanation: Subject searching retrieves catalogue records associated with a topic or subject heading.

questions.question_text: Which catalogue field is useful when the exact name of a book is known?
questions.explanation: A title search is appropriate when the exact or partial title is known.

questions.question_text: Why is keyword searching often broader than subject-heading searching?

options.label: A
options.text: Keywords may occur in several record fields and are not limited to controlled vocabulary

questions.explanation: Keyword searches may match words across titles, subjects, notes, and other fields.

questions.question_text: A dictionary is mainly used to find:
questions.explanation: Dictionaries provide definitions, spelling, pronunciation, and usage information.

questions.question_text: An encyclopedia is useful for:

options.label: A
options.text: Obtaining background information on a topic

questions.explanation: Encyclopedias provide introductory or overview information across subjects.

questions.question_text: Which source is most appropriate for locating geographical places?
questions.explanation: An atlas contains maps and geographical information.

questions.question_text: A bibliography is:

options.label: A
options.text: A list of books or other sources

questions.explanation: A bibliography lists sources relating to a work, author, or subject.

questions.question_text: A thesaurus is particularly useful for finding:
questions.explanation: A thesaurus provides synonyms, antonyms, and semantically related words.

questions.question_text: A student beginning research on an unfamiliar topic should often start with:

options.label: A
options.text: A reliable overview or reference source

questions.explanation: Reliable reference sources provide foundational context and vocabulary for deeper research.

questions.question_text: Information retrieval refers to:

options.label: A
options.text: Finding relevant information from organised sources

questions.explanation: Information retrieval involves locating information that matches a user's need.

questions.question_text: Which search term combination is likely to produce more focused results?
questions.explanation: Combining specific concepts narrows retrieval toward relevant records.

questions.question_text: The Boolean operator AND generally:

options.label: A
options.text: Narrows a search by requiring both terms

options.label: B
options.text: Expands a search to unrelated topics

questions.explanation: AND retrieves records containing all specified concepts.

questions.question_text: The Boolean operator OR is useful for:
questions.explanation: OR broadens retrieval by accepting either of the connected terms.

questions.question_text: Quotation marks in many search systems are used to:
questions.explanation: Quotation marks commonly tell a search engine to preserve phrase order.

questions.question_text: A student searching 'renewable energy Nigeria' receives thousands of results. Which action would best improve precision?

options.label: A
options.text: Add more specific concepts related to the research question

questions.explanation: Adding relevant concepts narrows the result set toward the specific information need.

questions.question_text: A study timetable is useful because it:

options.label: A
options.text: Helps allocate time systematically to academic tasks

questions.explanation: A timetable helps organise available time around priorities and study goals.

questions.question_text: Which study method is generally more effective for long-term retention?

options.label: B
options.text: One very long session before the examination

questions.explanation: Spaced practice distributes learning over time and supports durable retention.

questions.question_text: Active recall involves:

options.label: A
options.text: Trying to retrieve information from memory

questions.explanation: Active recall strengthens memory by practising retrieval rather than recognition alone.

questions.question_text: A realistic study goal should be:
questions.explanation: Specific achievable goals provide direction and allow progress to be monitored.

questions.question_text: The Pomodoro-style approach is based on:

options.label: A
options.text: Alternating focused work periods with short breaks

questions.explanation: Time-blocking methods such as Pomodoro divide work into focused intervals separated by breaks.

questions.question_text: Which strategy best addresses procrastination on a large assignment?

options.label: A
options.text: Break the task into smaller scheduled steps and begin with a manageable action

options.label: B
options.text: Wait until the deadline becomes urgent

options.label: D
options.text: Attempt the whole project without planning

questions.explanation: Breaking large tasks into manageable steps reduces friction and makes progress easier to start.

questions.question_text: Good notes should mainly capture:

options.label: A
options.text: Key ideas and important supporting details

questions.explanation: Effective notes focus on the main ideas and useful supporting information.

questions.question_text: Skimming is used mainly to:

options.label: A
options.text: Obtain the general idea of a text quickly

questions.explanation: Skimming is rapid reading for overall meaning and structure.

questions.question_text: Scanning is used mainly to:
questions.explanation: Scanning is used to locate specific items such as names, dates, or keywords.

questions.question_text: A concept map helps students:
questions.explanation: Concept maps visually organise ideas and the connections between them.

questions.question_text: Paraphrasing involves:

options.label: A
options.text: Restating an idea in new wording while preserving its meaning

questions.explanation: Paraphrasing expresses source material genuinely in different wording.

questions.question_text: Why is reviewing notes shortly after a lecture useful?

options.label: A
options.text: It helps reinforce learning and identify missing or unclear points while the material is still fresh

options.label: B
options.text: It guarantees all notes are correct

questions.explanation: Early review strengthens memory and allows unclear sections to be corrected while recall is fresh.

questions.question_text: The main purpose of a citation is to:

options.label: A
options.text: Acknowledge the source of information or ideas

questions.explanation: Citations credit sources and allow readers to trace supporting material.

questions.question_text: A reference list normally contains:
questions.explanation: A reference list identifies works cited in the academic document.

questions.question_text: Why should direct quotations usually include a citation?

options.label: A
options.text: Because the exact words come from another source

questions.explanation: Directly reproduced words must be attributed to their original source.

questions.question_text: Which information is commonly required when referencing a book?

options.label: A
options.text: Author, title, publication details, and year

questions.explanation: Book references normally identify the author, title, publisher information, and publication year.

questions.question_text: Consistent referencing style is important because it:

options.label: A
options.text: Makes source information clear and predictable

options.label: B
options.text: Changes the facts in the source

questions.explanation: Consistency helps readers interpret citations and locate sources efficiently.

questions.question_text: A student paraphrases an author's argument but provides no citation. Why can this still be plagiarism?

options.label: A
options.text: The underlying idea still belongs to the original author and requires acknowledgement

options.label: D
options.text: The words are different, so ownership no longer matters

questions.explanation: Paraphrasing changes wording, not ownership of the underlying idea.

topics.name: Academic Integrity and Ethical Information Use

questions.question_text: Plagiarism is:

options.label: A
options.text: Presenting another person's work or ideas without proper acknowledgement

questions.explanation: Plagiarism misrepresents another person's intellectual work as one's own.

questions.question_text: Which practice demonstrates academic integrity?

options.label: A
options.text: Citing sources used in an assignment

questions.explanation: Proper attribution is a core element of academic integrity.

questions.question_text: Fabrication in academic work means:
questions.explanation: Fabrication involves making up data, results, or sources that do not exist.

questions.question_text: Collusion becomes academically improper when students:

options.label: A
options.text: Cooperate on work that is required to be completed independently

questions.explanation: Unauthorised collaboration on independently assessed work can constitute academic misconduct.

questions.question_text: Copyright is relevant to students because it:

options.label: A
options.text: Protects creators' rights over original works

options.label: B
options.text: Makes all online material free to copy

questions.explanation: Copyright protects original creative works and governs how they may be copied or reused.

questions.question_text: Which action best demonstrates ethical use of online information?

options.label: A
options.text: Evaluate the source, respect usage rights, and provide attribution where required

options.label: B
options.text: Copy material because it is publicly accessible

options.label: C
options.text: Remove the author's name before submission

options.label: D
options.text: Assume every website is public domain

questions.explanation: Online availability does not remove intellectual-property or attribution obligations.
